extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and advanced graduate students working in arithmetic geometry / Mochizuki's IUT theory
extracted.subtask_description: Expository/motivational discussion of Mochizuki's (cid:2)-link, multiradial algorithm, and related comparison theorems (Hodge, p-adic Hodge, Hodge–Arakelov) in the context of the IUT approach to the abc conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariance and compatibility for log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that log-volumes are invariant under (Indet xy), (Indet !), and also compatible with log-Kummer correspondence of Theorem 13.12 (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log-volume computations used in the arguments must be carried out in ways that are invariant under the listed indeterminacies and compatible with the log-Kummer correspondence; this compatibility is invoked repeatedly when comparing different 'ways' of computing log-volumes of q-pilot objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admitting indeterminacies to obtain LGP-link
rubrics_metrics.description: By admitting (Indet xy), (Indet !), and (Indet ") we obtain (cid:2)(cid:22) LGP-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction of the LGP-link relies on allowing specified indeterminacies; these indeterminacies are treated as part of the geometry (they are not obstructions but structural features used to relate objects across different 'scheme theories').

rubrics_metrics.name: Permutative, horizontal, and vertical indeterminacies (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indet xy: the permutative indeterminacy in the (cid:19)etale transport; Indet !: the horizontal indeterminacy in the Kummer detachment (with integral structures); Indet ": the vertical indeterminacy in the Kummer detachment (descent data from Z to F1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three named indeterminacies are the primary kinds that must be allowed/controlled in the IUT constructions and appear explicitly in diagrammatic comparisons; understanding their roles is necessary for following and reproducing the constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological two-way computation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The tautological two ways of computations of log-volumes of q-pilot objects (via Kummer detachment and via log-Kummer correspondence) correspond to computations of self-intersection numbers of the diagonal Z over F1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing the two computation routes one must track the same arithmetic/geometric object seen in two scheme-theoretic incarnations; the equivalence (up to allowed indeterminacies) is used to derive inequalities relevant to heights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The crucial cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments (Theorem 7.23 (1)) is required for Kummer compatibility of theta monoids; this rigidity uses the quadraticity of the commutator [ ; ] structure of the theta group (Heisenberg group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any variant of the (cid:2)-link construction that destroys cyclotomic rigidity (for example, replacing (cid:2) by (cid:2)^N with N>1) will fail to preserve necessary Kummer compatibilities; so constructions must preserve the quadratic commutator structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant-multiple rigidity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The crucial constant multiple rigidity of mono-theta environments (Theorem 7.23 (3)) must hold; replacing (cid:2) by (cid:2)^N (N>1) breaks this rigidity because N-th power maps produce mutually non-isomorphic line bundles and yield constant-multiple indeterminacies under inner automorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reduce indeterminacies to acceptable ('mild') ones one needs constant-multiple rigidity; variants that introduce constant-multiple ambiguities obstruct the mono-anabelian reconstruction steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order-of-zero at cusps constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: If we replace (cid:2) by (cid:2)^N (N>1), then the order of zero of (cid:2)^N at cusps equals N>1 and a Kummer correspondence loop creates an N-power map which causes the log-Kummer correspondence to collapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining order-of-zero = 1 (no unwanted high-order zeros at cusps) is essential for preserving the log-Kummer correspondence; variants that increase orders break the correspondence and ruin the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masser's lower bound obstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the N>1 variant worked, one would obtain an inequality ht . (1/N)(1+(cid:15))(log-diff + log-cond) for N>1, which contradicts Masser’s lower bound in analytic number theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposed modification of the core construction must not produce consequences that violate known analytic lower bounds (e.g., Masser); such contradictions rule out certain variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to control and reduce indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: We need not only to reconstruct (up to some indeterminacies) mathematical objects in the scheme theory of one side of a (cid:2)-link from the ones in the scheme theory of the other side, but also to reduce the indeterminacies to mild ones. In order to do so, we need to control them, to reduce them by some rigidities, to kill them by some operations like taking p-adic logarithms for the roots of unity, to estimate them by considering that some images are contained in some containers even though they are not precisely determinable, and to synchronise some indeterminacies to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful application of the multiradial algorithm requires a toolbox: use rigidities (cyclotomic, constant-multiple), p-adic logarithms, container estimates, and synchronization lemmas to reduce indeterminacies to terms bounded by log-diff + log-cond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial algorithm goal and admissible error
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiradial algorithm allows us to compare degrees of arithmetic line bundles arising in different 'arithmetically holomorphic structures' (scheme theories) sharing an underlying analytic structure, after admitting mild indeterminacies. Concrete calculations show the indeterminacies are (roughly) log-diff + log-cond, yielding inequalities of the form 0 . (large number) ((cid:25) ht) and ultimately ht . log-diff + log-cond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm's correctness depends on being able to bound all arising indeterminacies by explicit arithmetic error-terms (log-diff + log-cond) and to ensure these errors are small relative to the main terms when parameters (like l) are large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hodge–Arakelov comparison prerequisites (discretised analogue)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Hodge–Arakelov setup: let E be an elliptic curve over a number field F, l>2 a prime, assume a nontrivial 2-torsion point P in E(F)[2] (or similar torsion of order prime to l), write L=O(l[P]). Then the main theorem says the evaluation map on Ey[l] is an isomorphism of F-vector spaces and preserves specified integral structures at places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To apply the discretised Hodge–Arakelov comparison one needs appropriate torsion structure (e.g., a rational 2-torsion point or other torsion prime to l), choices of line bundles L, and careful integral-structure bookkeeping at all places; the degree computations on both sides feed into the later arithmetic inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothetical global multiplicative subspace (and workaround)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a global multiplicative subspace M ⊂ E[l] of rank 1 existed (coinciding with the multiplicative subspace at each non-Archimedean bad place), then a simple Hodge–Arakelov projection would yield an inclusion q OK ,! q^{j^2} OK leading to a direct height bound. Since such a global multiplicative subspace does not exist in general, Mochizuki instead constructs an analogue 'outside' scheme theory via the (cid:2)-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One should not expect a global scheme-theoretic multiplicative subspace in general; the IUT approach circumvents this by defining and comparing appropriate objects outside the classical scheme-theoretic category and then controlling the resulting indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition C.1 — height-counting finiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L be an arithmetic line bundle such that L_Q is ample. Then for any degree d and real C we have finitely many rational points: # {x ∈ X(Q) of degree d | ht_L(x) ≤ C} < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard arithmetic-geometry finiteness (height counting) statement is used to reduce arguments to projective-space embeddings and to control the number of points of bounded height—used as a prerequisite in several reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem C.2 — non-critical Belyi map existence criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a proper smooth connected curve X/Q and finite disjoint sets S,T ⊂ X(Q) (S ∩ T = ∅), there exists a morphism β : X → P^1_Q unramified over P^1_Q  0,1,∞g such that (a) β is unramified over P^1_Q  0,1,∞g, (b) β(S) ⊂ {0,1,∞}, and (c) β(T) ⊂ P^1(Q)  0,1,∞g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce a Belyi map that maps specified rational points into {0,1,∞} while keeping another set T mapped to Q-points outside those three values, one follows the explicit multi-step construction given (adjoining points, choosing sections, rational transformations and induction on fields of definition); these are constructive existence criteria used in further propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem B.1 — relative Grothendieck conjecture (bijectivity conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K be a sub-p-adic field, X a smooth pro-variety over K, and Y a hyperbolic pro-curve over K. Then the natural maps Hom_dom_K(X,Y) → Hom_open^{GK}((π_1^arith X),(π_1^arith Y))/Inn(π_1^geom Y) → Hom_open^{GK}((π_1^arith X)^(p),(π_1^arith Y)^(p)) are bijective; similarly for isomorphism parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relative anabelian bijectivity is a structural criterion ensuring that (under the stated hypotheses) morphisms (or isomorphisms) of varieties are recovered from open continuous GK-equivariant homomorphisms of their arithmetic fundamental groups; it underpins many reconstruction steps in IUT-style arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma C.3 — k-core obstruction for semi-elliptic orbicurves
rubrics_metrics.description: If a semi-elliptic orbicurve X over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0 has a nontrivial automorphism then it does not admit a k-core; moreover there are precisely four isomorphism classes of semi-elliptic orbicurves over k which do not admit k-core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural classification result is used when reasoning about possible core objects in anabelian reconstructions and indicates precise exceptions to the existence of k-cores that must be respected in any argument invoking cores.
